title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which of these most clearly separates an agent from a workflow, when both use a language model?

options.text: An agent runs on a larger model than a workflow does
In an agent the model chooses the next step, not the code
An agent can call tools, while a workflow cannot call any
A workflow repeats in a loop, while an agent runs one pass

items.stem: Which task for the makerspace assistant most needs an agent, because no one can say in advance which steps it will take?

options.text: Sending a confirmation message each time a booking is saved
Posting the day's machine schedule to the lab board at 8 am
Helping a student find out why their 3D prints keep warping
Turning a student's booking request into a calendar entry

items.stem: Whenever a booking is confirmed, the assistant must check the student's training record, then save the booking, then send a confirmation, always in that order. What is the best design for this part?

options.text: A fixed workflow in code that runs the three steps in order
An agent, so that the model picks the order of steps each time
An agent, because only an agent can call the three tools
Three separate agents, each one responsible for a single step

items.stem: Your code always calls search_manuals once with the student's question, passes the top pages to the model, and shows the model's answer. The model never chooses a tool. Is this an agent or a workflow? Answer with one word.
For a task whose steps never change, why does a fixed workflow usually cost less per request than an agent?

options.text: A workflow always runs on a cheaper model than an agent
A workflow never needs to call a language model at all
A workflow uses tools that are free, unlike an agent's
A workflow needs no model calls to decide the next step

items.stem: A fixed workflow answers a manual question with 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 5 model calls per request. Assume every call costs the same. Over a week of 200 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?
